title: A Rivergate for the Escarpment
premise: Cyrus Kavanagh, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries for a rescue that went wrong, is running cargo down the Rivergate when the monsoon floods wash up a chest bearing the seal of Vessia, a nation erased from the maps twenty years ago. Inside are ledgers proving the border war that destroyed Vessia was manufactured by the very officials who now hunt Cyrus's name. Pursued by a magistrate who wants the chest and a Vessian exile who wants justice, Cyrus must decide whether to keep moving or finally stand still long enough to fight. She ends the monsoon by delivering the ledgers to a tribunal at the escarpment crossing, buying Vessia back its place on the map—and herself a country to belong to.
about_author: Astrid Montrose is the pen name of a former river pilot who spent six seasons navigating monsoon waterways before turning to fiction. Her novels blend hard-edged adventure with quiet interrogations of exile, borders, and the people maps forget.

chapters.title: Water That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Running late-season cargo down the swollen Rivergate, Cyrus navigates floodwater and hostile checkpoints, establishing her rule: never stop anywhere longer than a tide. When the river spits a sodden chest against her hull, she nearly lets it drift on—until she sees the Vessian seal. Emotional beat: restless competence shadowed by loneliness; curiosity overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Dead Nation's Stamp
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Hiding in a reed marsh, Cyrus pries open the chest: ledgers, letters, and orders proving Vessia's destruction was engineered for mining rights. She knows what documents like these do to people who carry them. A patrol skiff passes too close. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant responsibility—the past has literally washed into her hands.

chapters.title: A Stranger with a Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya. Ilya Vosk, a Vessian exile turned ferryman, spots Cyrus's campfire and recognizes the seal instantly. He offers his leaking boat and his life's knowledge of the river in exchange for a share of the truth. Cyrus refuses; he follows anyway. Emotional beat: wary friction between two people who've both survived by not trusting anyone.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Warrant
chapters.summary: POV: Magistrate Corven. Corven, whose career was built on the Vessian settlement, learns the chest surfaced and issues a sweeping warrant naming an unidentified woman. His subordinate hesitates at the warrant's breadth; Corven reminds him what happens to careers that hesitate. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace—power exercised as routine paperwork.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The storm makes landfall early. Cyrus and Ilya shelter in a drowned chapel where he reads her fragments of the ledgers aloud—names, villages, a forged attack that started the war. For the first time she sees the chest as people, not cargo. Emotional beat: grief breaking through cynicism; the beginning of belonging.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Corven's men burn the river settlements looking for them, and a harbor master who once sheltered Cyrus is arrested for it. Cyrus realizes her invisibility has always been paid for by others. She and Iyla plan the run to the escarpment tribunal before the flood season closes the crossing. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into resolve—staying invisible is no longer neutral.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Road
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya. Iyla leads them up the old Vessian trade road through landslides and a checkpoint ambush. He reveals he was a child soldier in the manufactured war and needs the ledgers read publicly, not just delivered. They argue over whether justice can come from the same courts that buried it. Emotional beat: hope colliding with justified bitterness.

chapters.title: Corven's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Corven. Cornering Cyrus at a river fork, Corven offers her a clean passport and a new name in exchange for the chest—and reveals he knows about the rescue that got her blacklisted, twisting the knife. She pretends to consider. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by old wounds; power corrupting through kindness as much as force.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Climax. In the last window before the peak flood closes the escarpment crossing, Cyrus runs the rapids with Iyla and the chest while Corven's gunboats close in. The leaking boat nearly founders; Iyla takes a bullet shielding the ledgers. Cyrus beaches at the tribunal steps as Corven's own clerk defects, carrying the documents inside. Emotional beat: white-knuckle sacrifice—everything risked for one moment of standing still.

chapters.title: A Rivergate for the Escarpment
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Resolution. The tribunal opens an inquiry; Corven's coalition fractures as the ledgers circulate. Vessia's restoration will take years, but the first map amendment is drafted. Iyla recovers and asks Cyrus to stay as guide for returning exiles. She unpacks her bag for the first time in a decade. Emotional beat: earned belonging—justice begun, home chosen at last.
